newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Crude build a wash in bearish API report.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Crude build a wash in bearish API report.

text.p: This week's inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) failed to provide fireworks to stoke oil markets out of recent bearish doldrums, or for that matter, push them into deeper hibernation.
Traders dismissed a voluminous 6.06 million barrel build in crude stocks, noting that once the West Coast was peeled out of that figure, it came in at a paltry 47,000 barrels.
"This week's report doesn't mean anything," said Thomas Blakeslee, an analyst with Cargill Investor Services in New York, echoing other players.

Crude stocks stood at 295.8 million barrels at the end of last week, though refinery utilization rates rose 1.2 percentage points to 90.3 percent amid views some refinery units that were down for maintenance came back into service.

Sources noted an interesting sidebar to the report was the fact that while distillate stocks fell by a surprising 4.1 million barrels, they were, for the first time since June 1995, above year-ago levels.
"Despite the big draw on distillates, the year-on-year comparison makes it a pretty bearish report. "I'd sell heating oil on this news."

"A few months ago, no one would have guessed that distillate stocks would be higher than a year ago. This was not expected," said John Lichtblau, president of Petroleum Industry Research Foundation in New York.

Still ACCESS traders were trying to push up March heating oil on the API news, with some offers seen as high as 64.50 cents a gallon Tuesday evening -- up 0.32 from the daytime settlement. Stocks stood at 115.5 million barrels.
Some traders saw bullishness in the draw itself and in the fact that heating oil stocks in the big Northeast heating oil market remained 4.9 million barrels below last year.
But reactions to the crude data, and to the 2.9 million barrel build in gasoline stocks that brought unleaded inventories to 204.2 million barrels, were definitely bearish.
Crude oil for March delivery dipped about five cents from the earlier settlement of $24.02 a barrel, while March gasoline trimmed over 0.60 cent from the settlement price of 67.40 cents a gallon.
Despite that build in gasoline stocks, unleaded still appeared to be benefiting from fairly widespread views that gasoline was on the verge of a pre-spring run-up in price.
